narrative_purpose: A side-by-side natural water-mass comparison corrects the intuition that the clearest blue water must be the most biologically productive.
subject: One continuous ocean scene divided by a sinuous natural front. On the left, transparent cobalt-blue water admits deep shafts of light but contains only a few tiny plankton cells and scattered fish. On the right, a cooler green-teal plume contains dense microscopic producers, suspended particles, grazing specks and one compact school of small alien fish. The two water masses meet without a hard border.
scene: The upper open ocean near an unseen island, observed just below the surface across a biological front.
camera: Wide level underwater comparison view, clear oligotrophic water on the left and productive plume on the right, equal visual weight.
light: Long clean cyan shafts penetrate the clear side; the productive side scatters softer green-teal light and becomes less transparent with depth.
palette: Cobalt indigo and cyan on the clear side, living teal and muted green-cyan on the productive side, sparse amber highlights on fish.
style: Painterly comparative naturalist plate with a physically continuous water front, not a split-screen graphic.
detail_level: Sparse left water, visibly particle-rich right water, microscopic texture and a legible fish aggregation; backgrounds remain simple for labels.
composition: A curved vertical front creates two readable halves. Preserve open upper corners and dark lower margins for annotation boxes.
consistency_notes: The productive water should look alive rather than dirty or toxic. Do not imply universal exact colours; this is a mechanism plate.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no split-screen border, no before-after captions, no sewage, no photographic or CGI look
